name: Limits meter
purpose: A READOUT OF AN ALLOWANCE AGAINST A CAP: how much of a payment, daily or monthly limit has been used, how much is left, when the allowance comes back, and — at the ceiling — what the user can no longer do. PROPOSED #209 (itinerary row 96, slug limits-meter, P3) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED. Fintech semantics are Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2).
$existenceQuestion: ⛔ READ FIRST, BECAUSE THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE FOUND IS EVIDENCE AGAINST THIS COMPONENT. progress-bar.meta.json relationships.commonPatterns reads VERBATIM: ['file upload progress', 'multi-part transfer progress', 'savings goal / limits meter', 'profile completeness score']. THE GATED PROGRESS-BAR ALREADY CLAIMS THIS PATTERN BY NAME, and its specimen 3 is a non-percentage determinate bar carrying its domain in aria-valuetext, which is geometrically a limits meter. The bar in this component is Progress-bar's, COPIED BYTE-FOR-BYTE; no bar geometry was drawn. What is arguably new is the READOUT: the cap, the reset horizon, the at-limit consequence and the stack. THREE LIVE OUTCOMES, ALL DAVE'S: keep it; merge it into Runway-bar as a parameterised 'allowance' mode; or delete it and use Progress-bar with a domain aria-valuetext. Deleting this pair of files costs nothing, because nothing registers them.

props.name: used
props.$note: The consumed part of the allowance. Bound to aria-valuenow.

props.name: cap
props.$note: The CEILING — bound to aria-valuemax. ⛔ Not a target: a target is a goal you are trying to reach, a cap is a boundary you are not allowed to cross. A limits meter that grows a target IS a Chart-bullet.

props.name: fillDirection
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (Q2). Drawn as USED — the bar fills as you spend, like every progress bar. The inverse, REMAINING (the bar empties, like a fuel gauge), is the other honest reading of a 'meter' and is what 'how much do I have left' actually asks. Dave's.

props.name: resetHorizon
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (Q5). 'Resets at midnight' / 'Resets 1 July'. Whether it belongs in the chip, in the caption, or in both is unruled — the reference draws it BOTH ways on different specimens so both are visible.

props.name: verdict
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (Q3). Rendered as a Status-indicator RAG-tint chip ALWAYS CARRYING ITS WORD. ⛔ 'at-limit' sits on the WARNING seat, not the error seat, even at 100% — deliberate restraint, NOT a considered ruling: the error seat touches the two-red law (s151-D1) and is Dave's.

props.name: consequence
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (Q7). The at-limit sentence ('You cannot make another transfer from this account until midnight'), role="status". Drawn stating it, because a number the user cannot act on is not an answer.

props.name: layout
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (Q6). Real limits come in SETS — per payment, per day, per month — and the set is the honest anatomy. The stack carries ONE role="group" label rather than three.

props.name: size
props.$note: 4px and 8px track heights — Progress-bar's own two sizes and its same token pair. Nothing new.

variants.name: within-limit
variants.use: The ordinary case. Ink on track, a success-tint chip carrying the reset time.

variants.name: approaching
variants.use: Nearly spent. The bar is longer and the WORD changed; the hue of the bar did not.

variants.name: at-limit
variants.use: The allowance is fully used. The bar is full because that is the honest geometry, and the consequence is a sentence. NO RED.

variants.name: stack
variants.use: Per payment · per day · per month under one group label, no chips.

variants.name: emphasis
variants.use: Progress-bar's 8px rule, for a region where the limit is the primary content.

tokens.fill: progress/complete — the used part. THEME INK in all four themes since s175-D1, exactly as Progress-bar binds it.
tokens.text: text/default — every figure and the consequence line
tokens.muted: text/secondary — labels, legend keys, the caption
tokens.border: border/subtle — the outline on the 'left' legend swatch, so an empty swatch is still a visible mark
tokens.status: rag/success + rag/success-tint | rag/warning + rag/warning-tint — the verdict chip, copied byte-for-byte from Runway-bar via Account-card
tokens.radius: border-radius/indicator — 0 in Mono and Legacy; Console forks through the cascade. Nothing is round except the 8px chip dot.
tokens.$note: NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED. Every value here already exists and is already bound by a gated component. ⛔ AND NO RAG COLOUR TOUCHES THE BAR IN ANY STATE — see $noRedInvented.

$noRedInvented: ⛔ THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS FILE. 'You have hit your daily limit' is where a critical red gets improvised. NONE IS. The bar is INK ON TRACK in every state including at-limit, inherited from the gated Progress-bar, whose own meta gives the reason in Dave's terms: 'Progress is STRUCTURE, not status (Dave 2026-07-21) — hence the ink pair rather than a RAG colour.' An amount used is a QUANTITY, so it takes the same treatment. The VERDICT is a separate object — a Status-indicator RAG-tint chip carrying a WORD and the reset time. Which verdict maps to which tint is a SEMANTIC binding and is DAVE'S, proposed not ruled, and the error seat is not taken even at 100%.

motion.entry: The fill's width transition only, over the inherited 140ms ease.
motion.reducedMotion: The fill still MOVES to its final position — the value must be reachable — it just arrives without an animated sweep (2.3.3 / 2.2.2). Progress-bar's own behaviour, copied, plus the global collapse.

responsive.rule: max-width 480px on the readout and on the stack; the head and the legend both wrap. No breakpoint switch and no container query — there is nothing to reflow. Verified in a real browser at 1400px, light and dark.

livesInside: Transfer / payment flows (before the amount is entered)
mustNotNeighbour: A Chart-bullet showing the same allowance against a target (a limit is not a target)
A second bar restating the same number in a different direction

accessibility.role: role="group" + aria-labelledby around each readout and around the stack; role="progressbar" on each bar with aria-valuenow / valuemin / valuemax and a domain-carrying aria-valuetext. Copied from Progress-bar via Runway-bar.
accessibility.openRoleQuestion: ⚠ INHERITED FROM Runway-bar #204 AND CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED, NOT RE-DECIDED: role="progressbar" vs role="meter". The search that fails to settle it was RE-RUN at #209 rather than cited (s202-D3): `grep -rln 'role="meter"' knowledge/snippets/` → two files, this one and Runway-bar, and every hit in both is PROSE not markup, i.e. ZERO of the 91 snippets uses the role; `grep -icE '\bmeter\b' knowledge/_rulings.json` → 0. Nothing in the store rules it. progressbar is used because the gated parent carries it; meter is arguably more correct for a gauge that is not task progress — and this component is literally called a meter. DAVE'S; if he rules 'meter', both files change together.
accessibility.consequence: The at-limit sentence is role="status" (polite): the limit was already reached, the user is reading, not being interrupted.
accessibility.notColourAlone: Three channels on every specimen: the verdict WORD in the chip, the arithmetic in text, and aria-valuetext on the bar. Remove all colour and the component still says everything it means (1.4.1).
accessibility.hitArea: PASSIVE — the component contains no interactive target, so the 44px minimum has no seat here. Declared rather than assumed (Runway-bar's precedent).

antiPatterns: ⛔ PAINTING THE BAR RED AT THE LIMIT. The bar is ink on track in every state. See $noRedInvented.
⛔ GROWING A TARGET MARKER OR QUALITATIVE BANDS. A limit is a ceiling, not a goal. With a target this IS a Chart-bullet and should be one.
⛔ DROPPING THE CAP, THE RESET AND THE CONSEQUENCE AND KEEPING THE BAR. Without them this IS a Progress bar and should be one — Progress-bar's own meta already claims the pattern by name.
Restating the same allowance twice in opposite directions (used AND remaining as two bars). Pick a direction — that choice is Q2, Dave's.
Relying on the chip DOT to convey the verdict. The dot is 1.98:1 / 2.18:1 standalone (measured #204); the word is the carrier.
Painting a delta or an arrow on this component. The two delta conventions question is OPEN AND DAVE'S and nothing here may settle it by construction.

provenance.$sourceNarrative: Itinerary row 96 ('Spend/transfer limit gauge.') via knowledge/_COMPONENT-LIBRARY-TARGET.md line 104, the Fintech-specific table, GAP · P2–P3. reviews/ITINERARY-STATUS-2026-08-19-v1.json records drift 'AGREES', all five slug probes negative, and names Chart-bullet as the related component ('Chart-bullet is a measure-vs-target gauge'). ⛔ THAT RELATION IS WRONG AND THE ADJUDICATION SAYS SO: a limit is a ceiling, not a target; the real parent is Progress-bar, whose own meta already lists 'savings goal / limits meter' in commonPatterns. Re-probed at #209 against the store itself: no snippet, meta, showroom page, MIGRATED_SNIPPETS entry or canon scope exists under this slug, and a direct grep of knowledge/_rulings.json for limit / allowance / cap / meter returns ZERO entries naming this component — UNRULED.

$differsFrom.Progress-bar: The BAR is Progress-bar, copied byte-for-byte; nothing was added at the bar level. THE TELL: progress is something you WANT to complete; a limit is something you must NOT complete. Identical geometry, inverted meaning — a full progress bar is success, a full limits meter is a BLOCKED PAYMENT. That inversion is the entire argument for a distinct component and it is an argument about MEANING, which is why it is Dave's to accept or reject.
$differsFrom.Chart-bullet: Chart-bullet compares a MEASURE to a TARGET against qualitative BANDS, as an SVG figure with a real dv-table, intent 'comparison'. This has no target, no bands, no SVG, no table and no dataviz series token. A target is a goal to reach; a limit is a ceiling not to cross.
$differsFrom.Runway-bar: The near-sibling, PROPOSED #204. Runway asks 'does my money cover what is scheduled, and until when?' — its maximum is my own BALANCE and its horizon is a date I DISCOVER. This asks 'how much am I ALLOWED to move, and when does the allowance come back?' — its maximum is a CAP set by the bank and its horizon is a repeating RESET known in advance. Runway's ceiling is a fact about my money; a limit's ceiling is a rule about my permission. Drawn to Runway-bar's own anatomy DELIBERATELY, so the two files already rhyme if Dave merges them.
$differsFrom.Account-card: Account-card states a balance. This states a permission. They are often on the same screen and must not be confused.

$decisionsForDave: ⛔ FIRST: should this exist at all? Progress-bar's meta already claims 'savings goal / limits meter' by name, and Runway-bar is a near-sibling. Keep / merge into Runway-bar / delete.
Does the bar fill with what is USED (as drawn) or empty with what REMAINS, like a fuel gauge?
The verdict vocabulary and its chip binding — and specifically whether 'at limit' belongs on the ERROR seat. Deliberately not taken; it touches the two-red law.
Does a healthy limit show a chip at all? Drawn both ways.
Where does the reset live — the chip, the caption, or both? Drawn both ways.
Is the component the SET of limits (per payment / per day / per month) or one bar a page repeats?
Should the meter state the at-limit consequence in a sentence, or only the number?
The 'Per payment' row renders as an empty track reading '£0 of £10,000 used' and always will — a per-payment cap never accumulates. Should it be a bar at all, or a plain stated rule?
role="progressbar" or role="meter"? Inherited from Runway-bar #204, still unruled; if you rule it, both components change together.
